teaser.en: Called the wild mango, it is actually a bean-family tree whose yellow fruit is eaten raw or cooked.

summary.en: *Mnyungwinyungwi*, the wild mango, is a big spreading tree of hot riverine and swamp forest with tasty yellow fruits. Its wood is carved into stools, mortars and drums.

about.en:
*Mnyungwinyungwi* is a large, spreading deciduous tree. Its leaves are made of many small leaflets dotted with tiny translucent spots, which show when a leaflet is held up to the light. The flowers have no showy petals; instead, bursts of yellow-orange stamens make the colour.

The fruit is yellow and fleshy. Despite the English name, the tree is not a mango but a member of the bean family.

where.en: It grows in riverine and swamp forest in the hot lowlands.

uses.en:
The fruit is tasty and is eaten raw or cooked.

The wood is used for stools, mortars and drums.

names.en: The ICRAF handbook gives the Digo name *mnyungwinyungwi*. In Swahili it is *mroma*, *mvoo* or *mtigonzi*. In English it is called the wild mango.

reason.en: The true mango it is named after
Another riverine tree of the bean family
Fruit tree also carved into stools and mortars
